newsitem.title: USA: Calif. voters OK tax reform, state bonds, wages.
newsitem.headline: Calif. voters OK tax reform, state bonds, wages.

text.p: Californians voted Tuesday to approve tax reform, two large statewide bond measures to fund water projects and aid for veterans, and to raise the state's minimum wage, according to election returns.
Voters approved an initiative that would require all local taxes to be submitted to voters for approval despite warnings that the measure would undermine local government finances.
With 100 percent of precincts reporting, Proposition 218 had the support of 56.4 percent of voters while 43.6 percent were opposed, state election officials said.

Proposition 204, which provides for a bond issue of $995 million to ensure safe drinking water, increase water supplies, clean up pollution in rivers and protect wildlife, was approved by a vote of 63 percent to 37 percent with 100 percent of precincts reporting, election officials said.

Proposition 206, which provides for a bond issue of $400 million to provide farm and home aid for California veterans, was approved by a vote of 53.7 percent to 46.3 percent with 100 percent of precincts reporting, officials said.

Proposition 210, which increases the state minimum wage for all industries to $5.00 per hour on March 1, 1997, and to $5.75 per hour on March 1, 1998, was approved by 61.7 percent of the vote versus 38.3 percent opposed.
Voters in the state also approved campaign contribution and spending limits.

Voters rejected proposition 205, a jail bond measure that would have provided for a bond issue of $700 million to provide funds for construction, renovation and replacement of local juvenile and adult correctional facilities.
Voters also rejected Proposition 217, a measure that would have retroactively reinstated the highest tax rates on taxpayers.
